claim: MjNhaP1 is an archaeal electroneutral Na+/H+-antiporter.
source: We examined substrate-induced conformational changes in MjNhaP1, an archaeal electroneutral Na+/H+-antiporter resembling the human antiporter NHE1, by electron crystallography of 2D crystals in a range of physiological pH and Na+ conditions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of MjNhaP1.

claim: MjNhaP1 resembles the human antiporter NHE1.
source: We examined substrate-induced conformational changes in MjNhaP1, an archaeal electroneutral Na+/H+-antiporter resembling the human antiporter NHE1, by electron crystallography of 2D crystals in a range of physiological pH and Na+ conditions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: In the absence of sodium, changes in pH had no major effect on MjNhaP1 conformation.
source: In the absence of sodium, changes in pH had no major effect.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Changes in Na+ concentration caused a marked conformational change in MjNhaP1 that was largely pH-independent.
source: By contrast, changes in Na+ concentration caused a marked conformational change that was largely pH-independent.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: MjNhaP1 shows approximately 10-fold stronger Na+ binding at pH 8 than at pH 4.
source: Crystallographically determined, apparent dissociation constants indicated ∼10-fold stronger Na+ binding at pH 8 than at pH 4, consistent with substrate competition for a common ion-binding site.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data in Figure 6.

claim: The pH-dependent Na+ binding in MjNhaP1 is consistent with substrate competition for a common ion-binding site.
source: Crystallographically determined, apparent dissociation constants indicated ∼10-fold stronger Na+ binding at pH 8 than at pH 4, consistent with substrate competition for a common ion-binding site.
evidence: This interpretation is stated in the abstract and supported by the experimental data.

claim: Projection difference maps indicated helix movements by about 2 Å in the 6-helix bundle region of MjNhaP1.
source: Projection difference maps indicated helix movements by about 2 Å in the 6-helix bundle region of MjNhaP1 that is thought to contain the ion translocation site.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by difference maps in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The 6-helix bundle region of MjNhaP1 is thought to contain the ion translocation site.
source: Projection difference maps indicated helix movements by about 2 Å in the 6-helix bundle region of MjNhaP1 that is thought to contain the ion translocation site.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is based on prior structural knowledge.

claim: The observed helix movements convert the antiporter from the proton-bound, outward-open state to the Na+-bound, inward-open state.
source: We propose that these movements convert the antiporter from the proton-bound, outward-open state to the Na+-bound, inward-open state.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism stated in the abstract based on the experimental observations.

claim: Oscillation between the two states would result in rapid Na+/H+ antiport.
source: Oscillation between the two states would result in rapid Na+/H+ antiport.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism stated in the abstract.

claim: Na+/H+ antiporters are ubiquitous and essential secondary-active transporters found in the cell membranes of all organisms.
source: Na+/H+ antiporters are ubiquitous and essential secondary-active transporters found in the cell membranes of all organisms.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Na+/H+ antiporters play crucial roles in the regulation of intracellular pH, sodium homeostasis, and cell volume.
source: They play crucial roles in the regulation of intracellular pH, sodium homeostasis, and cell volume.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: In humans, Na+/H+ antiporter dysfunction is associated with numerous serious or life-threatening diseases.
source: In humans, Na+/H+ antiporter dysfunction is associated with numerous serious or life-threatening diseases (Donowitz et al., 2013), which makes them important drug targets (Fliegel, 2009; Boedtkjer et al., 2012; Loo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Na+/H+ antiporters are important drug targets.
source: In humans, Na+/H+ antiporter dysfunction is associated with numerous serious or life-threatening diseases (Donowitz et al., 2013), which makes them important drug targets (Fliegel, 2009; Boedtkjer et al., 2012; Loo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Na+/H+ antiporters belong to the superfamily of cation/proton antiporters (CPA).
source: Na+/H+ antiporters belong to the superfamily of cation/proton antiporters (CPA), which include the CPA1 and CPA2 subfamilies as main branches (Brett et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The CPA superfamily includes the CPA1 and CPA2 subfamilies as main branches.
source: Na+/H+ antiporters belong to the superfamily of cation/proton antiporters (CPA), which include the CPA1 and CPA2 subfamilies as main branches (Brett et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: CPA1 transporters are electroneutral and most likely exchange protons and Na+ ions with a 1:1 stoichiometry.
source: CPA1 transporters are electroneutral and most likely exchange protons and Na+ ions with a 1:1 stoichiometry, whereas CPA2 transporters, which mostly exchange two protons per Na+, are electrogenic.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: CPA2 transporters mostly exchange two protons per Na+ and are electrogenic.
source: CPA1 transporters are electroneutral and most likely exchange protons and Na+ ions with a 1:1 stoichiometry, whereas CPA2 transporters, which mostly exchange two protons per Na+, are electrogenic.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The best-known member of the CPA2 subfamily is the Na+/H+ antiporter NhaA from E. coli.
source: The best-known member of the CPA2 subfamily is the Na+/H+ antiporter NhaA from E. coli.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: EcNhaA enables E. coli to survive at high salinity or alkaline pH.
source: EcNhaA enables E. coli to survive at high salinity or alkaline pH (Padan and Schuldiner, 1994), making use of the proton-motive force to extrude sodium from the cell (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: EcNhaA makes use of the proton-motive force to extrude sodium from the cell.
source: EcNhaA enables E. coli to survive at high salinity or alkaline pH (Padan and Schuldiner, 1994), making use of the proton-motive force to extrude sodium from the cell (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: EcNhaA exchanges one sodium ion against two protons.
source: (A) EcNhaA is a sodium pump driven by the proton-motive force, exchanging one sodium ion against two protons (Taglicht et al., 1991), enabling E. coli to survive at high sodium and alkaline pH.
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend and supported by a citation.

claim: MjNhaP1 is thought to act mainly as a proton pump driven by the sodium gradient, exchanging one proton against one sodium ion.
source: (B) MjNhaP1 is thought to act mainly as a proton pump driven by the sodium gradient, exchanging one proton against one sodium ion.
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend.

claim: MjNhaP1 plays a critical role in pH homeostasis.
source: Like the homologous NHE1 in mammals (Lee et al., 2012), MjNhaP1 plays a critical role in pH homeostasis and enables M. jannaschii to survive at low pH (4–6) and sodium concentrations up to 0.9 M (Jones et al., 1983; Hellmer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend and supported by citations.

claim: MjNhaP1 enables M. jannaschii to survive at low pH (4–6) and sodium concentrations up to 0.9 M.
source: Like the homologous NHE1 in mammals (Lee et al., 2012), MjNhaP1 plays a critical role in pH homeostasis and enables M. jannaschii to survive at low pH (4–6) and sodium concentrations up to 0.9 M (Jones et al., 1983; Hellmer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend and supported by citations.

claim: The archaeal CPA1 antiporters share significant sequence homology of functionally important regions with the mammalian NHE antiporters.
source: The archaeal CPA1 antiporters share significant sequence homology of functionally important regions with the mammalian NHE antiporters (Goswami et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: NHE1 transport activity shows a strong dependence on both H+ and Na+ concentrations.
source: A study of NHE1 in mammalian cells has shown a strong dependence of transport activity on both H+ and Na+ concentrations, with activity dropping to background level at pH 8, and a strong dependence on extracellular Na+ (Fuster et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: NHE1 activity drops to background level at pH 8.
source: A study of NHE1 in mammalian cells has shown a strong dependence of transport activity on both H+ and Na+ concentrations, with activity dropping to background level at pH 8, and a strong dependence on extracellular Na+ (Fuster et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: MjNhaP1 is thought to use a sodium gradient to extrude protons from the cell.
source: Like NHE1, but unlike EcNhaA, the Na+/H+ antiporter NhaP1 from Methanocaldoccocus jannaschii (MjNhaP1) is thought to use a sodium gradient to extrude protons from the cell (Figure 1) (Thauer et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: MjNhaP1 is active at pH 6.
source: Like NHE1 (Fuster et al., 2008), but again unlike EcNhaA, MjNhaP1 is active at pH 6, and down-regulated at pH 7.5 or above (Hellmer et al., 2002; Goswami et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: MjNhaP1 is down-regulated at pH 7.5 or above.
source: Like NHE1 (Fuster et al., 2008), but again unlike EcNhaA, MjNhaP1 is active at pH 6, and down-regulated at pH 7.5 or above (Hellmer et al., 2002; Goswami et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The first insight into the structure of a Na+/H+ antiporter came from the 3D map of the EcNhaA dimer in the membrane at 7 Å resolution.
source: The first insight into the structure of a Na+/H+ came from the 3D map of the EcNhaA dimer in the membrane at 7 Å resolution, obtained by electron crystallography of 2D crystals (Williams, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The EcNhaA map revealed 12 transmembrane α-helices (TMHs) per protomer.
source: The map revealed 12 transmembrane α-helices (TMHs) per protomer, referred to as TMH I-XII.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction based on prior structural work.

claim: The TMHs of EcNhaA were arranged in two groups: a 6-helix bundle at the tip of each protomer, and a row of 6 helices at the dimer interface.
source: The TMHs of EcNhaA were arranged in two groups: a 6-helix bundle at the tip of each protomer, and a row of 6 helices at the dimer interface.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction based on prior structural work.

claim: The 3.45 Å X-ray structure of monomeric EcNhaA showed an inward-open conformation.
source: The 3.45 Å X-ray structure of monomeric EcNhaA in an inward-open conformation provided further details, including a pair of discontinuous helices (TMH IV and XI) in the 6-helix bundle that were proposed to harbor the ion translocation site (Hunte et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: EcNhaA contains a pair of discontinuous helices (TMH IV and XI) in the 6-helix bundle that were proposed to harbor the ion translocation site.
source: The 3.45 Å X-ray structure of monomeric EcNhaA in an inward-open conformation provided further details, including a pair of discontinuous helices (TMH IV and XI) in the 6-helix bundle that were proposed to harbor the ion translocation site (Hunte et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: A 3D map of the MjNhaP1 dimer in the membrane at 7 Å resolution indicated 13 TMHs.
source: By electron crystallography we obtained a projection structure (Vinothkumar et al., 2005) and, more recently, a 3D map of the MjNhaP1 dimer in the membrane at 7 Å resolution (Goswami et al., 2011) that indicated 13 TMHs, referred to as TMHs 1-13.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The dimer interface of MjNhaP1 looked very different to that of EcNhaA.
source: While the dimer interface looked very different to that of EcNhaA, the structure of the 6-helix bundle was similar, supporting the notion of related transport mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction based on prior structural work.

claim: The structure of the 6-helix bundle in MjNhaP1 was similar to that of EcNhaA.
source: While the dimer interface looked very different to that of EcNhaA, the structure of the 6-helix bundle was similar, supporting the notion of related transport mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction based on prior structural work.

claim: Two-dimensional (2D) crystals are ideal for investigating conformational changes of membrane proteins in a native-like lipid environment.
source: Two-dimensional (2D) crystals are ideal for investigating conformational changes of membrane proteins in a native-like lipid environment (Subramaniam et al., 1993; Beroukhim and Unwin, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Substrate-induced changes in MjNhaP1 were discovered by electron crystallography of 2D crystals.
source: By this approach we discovered substrate-induced changes in MjNhaP1 (Vinothkumar et al., 2005) and in EcNhaA (Appel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Substrate-induced changes in EcNhaA were discovered by electron crystallography of 2D crystals.
source: By this approach we discovered substrate-induced changes in MjNhaP1 (Vinothkumar et al., 2005) and in EcNhaA (Appel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In both MjNhaP1 and EcNhaA, substrate-induced changes occurred in the 6-helix bundle.
source: In both cases, the changes occurred in the 6-helix bundle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction based on prior work.

claim: MjNhaP1 was purified and crystallized under Na+-free conditions.
source: For electron crystallography, MjNhaP1 was purified and crystallized under Na+-free conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental approach.

claim: The 2D crystals of MjNhaP1 grown under Na+-free conditions were more highly ordered than those obtained earlier, diffracting up to 6 Å resolution.
source: The 2D crystals looked similar to those obtained earlier (Vinothkumar et al., 2005; Goswami et al., 2011) but were more highly ordered, diffracting up to 6 Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by experimental data.

claim: 29 data sets of MjNhaP1 at different pH and salt concentrations were collected, processed and analyzed.
source: In total, 29 data sets of MjNhaP1 at different pH and salt concentrations were collected, processed and analyzed (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental work.

claim: Peaks in the projection maps characteristic of membrane-spanning helices at 6 Å resolution were observed in the two protomers of the crystallographic MjNhaP1 dimer.
source: Peaks in the projection maps characteristic of membrane-spanning helices at 6 Å resolution were observed in the two protomers of the crystallographic MjNhaP1 dimer (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The 7 Å 3D EM model of MjNhaP1 enabled assignment of peaks in the projection maps to the TMHs.
source: The 7 Å 3D EM model of MjNhaP1 (Goswami et al., 2011) enabled us to assign peaks in the projection maps to the TMHs and to the cytoplasmic (c) or exoplasmic (e) halves of the discontinuous TMHs 5 (5c/5e) and 12 (12c/12e) in the protomer (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 2.

claim: TMH 1-3 and 7-10 form the dimer interface in MjNhaP1.
source: TMH 1-3 and 7-10 form the dimer interface.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the structural model.

claim: 2D crystals grown without Na+ were incubated on the EM grid with sodium-free buffers at pH 4, 6 or 8 to observe pure pH-induced conformational changes.
source: To observe pure pH-induced conformational changes, 2D crystals grown without Na+ were incubated on the EM grid with sodium-free buffers at pH 4, 6 or 8 (Figure 3; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental approach.

claim: The resulting projection maps indicated only minor differences in the shape or position of density peaks upon pH changes in the absence of Na+.
source: The resulting projection maps indicated only minor differences in the shape or position of density peaks.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: A small positive peak close to TMH 10 was observed upon a shift from pH 4 or pH 8 to pH 6.
source: A small positive peak close to TMH 10 was observed upon a shift from pH 4 or pH 8 to pH 6 (Figure 3A,B) and a similarly-sized negative difference peak close to TMH 6 occurred in the transition from pH 8 to pH 6.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Differences between pH 4 and pH 8 without Na+ were at background level.
source: Differences between pH 4 and pH 8 without Na+ were at background level (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Addition of Na+ at pH 8 caused evident changes in the 6-helix bundle.
source: Addition of Na+ at pH 8 caused evident changes in the 6-helix bundle (Figure 4A), giving rise to major peaks in the difference maps (Figures 4C and 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The unit cell changed gradually from 81.2 × 104.2 Å to 80.6 × 107.9 Å at 500 mM Na+.
source: The unit cell changed gradually from 81.2 × 104.2 Å to 80.6 × 107.9 Å at 500 mM Na+, whereas a pH shift in the absence of salt had no significant effect on the unit cell dimensions (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and documented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: A pH shift in the absence of salt had no significant effect on the unit cell dimensions.
source: The unit cell changed gradually from 81.2 × 104.2 Å to 80.6 × 107.9 Å at 500 mM Na+, whereas a pH shift in the absence of salt had no significant effect on the unit cell dimensions (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and documented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: All difference maps at pH 8 showed the same three sets of positive/negative difference peaks.
source: All difference maps at pH 8 showed the same three sets of positive/negative difference peaks, outlined by ovals in Figure 5A.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Difference peaks within each set became progressively stronger as the NaCl concentration increased from 20 mM to 500 mM at pH 8.
source: Difference peaks within each set became progressively stronger as the NaCl concentration increased from 20 mM to 500 mM.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: At 20 mM NaCl at pH 8, there were 7–9 contour levels between the lowest negative and highest positive peaks in each set.
source: At 20 mM, there were 7–9 contour levels between the lowest negative and highest positive peaks in each set, rising to a peak-to-trough difference of 15 contour levels at 500 mM NaCl (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: At 500 mM NaCl at pH 8, there was a peak-to-trough difference of 15 contour levels.
source: At 20 mM, there were 7–9 contour levels between the lowest negative and highest positive peaks in each set, rising to a peak-to-trough difference of 15 contour levels at 500 mM NaCl (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A positive peak that was not matched by a corresponding negative peak appeared at 100 mM NaCl and above at pH 8.
source: A positive peak that was not matched by a corresponding negative peak appeared at 100 mM NaCl and above (Figure 5A), indicating a gain of order in this protein region.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The unmatched positive peak at 100 mM NaCl and above indicates a gain of order in this protein region.
source: A positive peak that was not matched by a corresponding negative peak appeared at 100 mM NaCl and above (Figure 5A), indicating a gain of order in this protein region.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Control experiments gave similar results for Na+ and Li+, which are both substrate ions of MjNhaP1.
source: Control experiments gave similar results for Na+ and Li+, which are both substrate ions of MjNhaP1, whereas Mg2+, which is not transported, did not give rise to significant difference peaks under otherwise similar conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mg2+, which is not transported by MjNhaP1, did not give rise to significant difference peaks.
source: Control experiments gave similar results for Na+ and Li+, which are both substrate ions of MjNhaP1, whereas Mg2+, which is not transported, did not give rise to significant difference peaks under otherwise similar conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: K+, which is not transported but has been reported to bind to EcNhaA, caused changes above background level that were different from those observed with Na+ or Li+.
source: K+, which is likewise not transported but has been reported to bind to EcNhaA (Alhadeff et al., 2011), caused changes above background level that were however different from those observed with Na+ or Li+ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The strong changes observed with Na+ or Li+ are substrate-specific.
source: The strong changes observed with Na+ or Li+ are thus substrate-specific.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the control experiments.

claim: At pH 4, essentially the same pattern of difference peaks and changes in unit cell dimensions were found as at pH 8.
source: At pH 4, essentially the same pattern of difference peaks and changes in unit cell dimensions were found as at pH 8 (Supplementary file 1 and Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At pH 4, the differences occurred at NaCl concentrations that were roughly 10-fold higher than at pH 8.
source: However, these differences occurred at NaCl concentrations that were roughly 10-fold higher than at pH 8 (Figures 5 and 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Difference maps at 20 or 100 mM NaCl at pH 4 were largely featureless, except for one comparatively weak pair at the position of the strongest peaks at higher NaCl concentration.
source: Difference maps at 20 or 100 mM NaCl at pH 4 were largely featureless, except for one comparatively weak pair (6 or 7 contour levels peak-to-trough) at the position of the strongest peaks at higher NaCl concentration (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At NaCl concentrations of 150 mM or above at pH 4, there was a broad difference peak to the left of the 6-helix bundle that was not observed at pH 8.
source: In addition, at NaCl concentrations of 150 mM or above, there was a broad difference peak to the left of the 6-helix bundle that was not observed at pH 8 (arrow in Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At pH 6, the same sets of difference peaks were evident, but only at elevated NaCl concentrations of 250 mM or above.
source: At pH 6, again the same sets of difference peaks were evident, but only at elevated NaCl concentrations of 250 mM or above (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: At pH 6, differences were much weaker (maximally 7–8 contour levels peak-to-trough) and more diffuse than at pH 8 or at pH 4.
source: Differences were much weaker (maximally 7–8 contour levels peak-to-trough) and more diffuse than at pH 8 or at pH 4 (Figure 5), even up to 1 M NaCl (not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Unit cell parameters at pH 6 did not change significantly.
source: Unit cell parameters at pH 6 did not change significantly (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and documented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Strong pairs of positive/negative peaks in projection difference maps at 6–8 Å resolution are indicative of helix movements.
source: Strong pairs of positive/negative peaks in projection difference maps at 6–8 Å resolution are indicative of helix movements, which can be either lateral displacement or helix tilts (Subramaniam et al., 1993; Appel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: The three sets of strong difference peaks in Figure 5 all map to the 6-helix bundle of MjNhaP1.
source: The three sets of strong difference peaks in Figure 5 all map to the 6-helix bundle of MjNhaP1 and indicate significant and specific rearrangements of TMHs in this part of the protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The three sets of strong difference peaks indicate significant and specific rearrangements of TMHs in the 6-helix bundle.
source: The three sets of strong difference peaks in Figure 5 all map to the 6-helix bundle of MjNhaP1 and indicate significant and specific rearrangements of TMHs in this part of the protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The changes take place in the physiological pH and Na+ concentration range for M. jannaschii.
source: The changes take place in the physiological pH and Na+ concentration range for M. jannaschii (Jones et al., 1983) and thus are likely to reflect the conformational changes in the transport cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The observed changes are likely to reflect the conformational changes in the transport cycle.
source: The changes take place in the physiological pH and Na+ concentration range for M. jannaschii (Jones et al., 1983) and thus are likely to reflect the conformational changes in the transport cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the data.

claim: The strongest pair of difference peaks (set 1) coincides with the projection of the cytoplasmic half of TMH 5 and the extracellular half of TMH 12 (helix segments 5c/12e).
source: Of the three sets of difference peaks in Figure 5 that are common to all three pH regimes, the strongest pair (set 1) coincides with the projection of the cytoplasmic half of TMH 5 and the extracellular half of TMH 12 (helix segments 5c/12e), indicating a joint movement of these two half helices.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The strongest pair of difference peaks indicates a joint movement of helix segments 5c and 12e.
source: Of the three sets of difference peaks in Figure 5 that are common to all three pH regimes, the strongest pair (set 1) coincides with the projection of the cytoplasmic half of TMH 5 and the extracellular half of TMH 12 (helix segments 5c/12e), indicating a joint movement of these two half helices.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Inspection of the corresponding peaks in the projection map and the 3D model indicates a displacement, most likely a lateral movement, of the 5c/12e helix pair by approximately 2 Å towards TMH 10 and 13.
source: Inspection of the corresponding peaks in the projection map (Figure 4) and the 3D model indicates a displacement, most likely a lateral movement, of the 5c/12e helix pair by ∼2 Å towards TMH 10 and 13.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The second-strongest pair of positive/negative difference peaks (set 2) maps to the projection of TMH 6.
source: The second-strongest pair of positive/negative difference peaks (set 2 in Figure 5) maps to the projection of TMH 6.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The peak corresponding to TMH 6 is elongated in the absence of Na+ and becomes round at elevated NaCl concentration, indicating that this helix reorients in response to Na+ binding.
source: In Figure 4, the peak corresponding to TMH 6 is elongated in the absence of Na+ and becomes round at elevated NaCl concentration, indicating that this helix reorients in response to Na+ binding.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the 3D model the extracellular half of TMH 6 is tilted, so that the entire TMH 6 becomes more straight and perpendicular to the membrane in response to Na+ binding.
source: In the 3D model the extracellular half of TMH 6 is tilted, so that the entire TMH 6 becomes more straight and perpendicular to the membrane in response to Na+ binding.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation based on the 3D model.

claim: The third set of difference peaks (set 3) coincides with the map region occupied by TMH 13 and helix 5e.
source: The third set of difference peaks in Figure 5 (set 3) coincides with the map region occupied by TMH 13 and helix 5e.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The projection peak corresponding to TMH 13 is more elongated at 500 mM NaCl than in absence of sodium, indicating that this helix becomes more tilted with increasing Na+ concentration.
source: The projection peak corresponding to TMH 13 is more elongated at 500 mM NaCl than in absence of sodium, indicating that this helix becomes more tilted with increasing Na+ concentration.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the projection maps.

claim: A peak for helix 5e is not evident at low Na+, but a clear peak is present at 100 mM NaCl and above in the projection maps.
source: A peak for helix 5e is not evident at low Na+, but a clear peak is present at 100 mM NaCl and above in the projection maps.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on inspection of the projection maps.

claim: Helix 5e is either highly tilted or disordered at low Na+.
source: Therefore helix 5e is either highly tilted or disordered at low Na+, which would both make it difficult to see in projection.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Upon Na+ binding, helix 5e either reorients or becomes ordered and then runs more or less perpendicular to the membrane plane.
source: Upon Na+ binding, it either reorients or becomes ordered and then runs more or less perpendicular to the membrane plane.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The broad difference peak to the left of the 6-helix bundle at pH 4 indicates a Na+-induced movement of the group of helices on the outside of the bundle, consisting of TMH 4, 11 and helix 12c.
source: The broad difference peak to the left of the 6-helix bundle in Figure 5C that appeared at pH 4 above 150 mM NaCl indicates a Na+-induced movement of the group of helices on the outside of the bundle, consisting of TMH 4, 11 and helix 12c.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Inspection of the corresponding projection maps indicates that this part of the bundle shifts by approximately 2 Å towards the dimer interface.
source: Again, inspection of the corresponding projection maps indicates that this part of the bundle shifts by ∼2 Å towards the dimer interface.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on inspection of the projection maps.

claim: This movement is largely absent at pH 8 or 6.
source: This movement is largely absent at pH 8 or 6.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison of the data.

claim: The positive difference peak above 100 mM NaCl at pH 8 or 250 mM at pH 4 indicates a gain of order in the region between the 6-helix bundle and of TMH 10.
source: The positive difference peak above 100 mM NaCl at pH 8 or 250 mM at pH 4 (Figure 5A,C) indicates a gain of order in the region between the 6-helix bundle and of TMH 10, which is part of the dimer interface.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: No significant differences were recorded in the central part of the dimer.
source: Otherwise, no significant differences were recorded in the central part of the dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the data.

claim: The E. coli antiporter NhaA shares many features with MjNhaP1.
source: The E. coli antiporter NhaA shares many features with MjNhaP1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Both EcNhaA and MjNhaP1 form dimers of similar shape and size in the membrane.
source: Both form dimers of similar shape and size in the membrane, and have the conserved 6-helix bundle thought to harbor the ion translocation site.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Both EcNhaA and MjNhaP1 have the conserved 6-helix bundle thought to harbor the ion translocation site.
source: Both form dimers of similar shape and size in the membrane, and have the conserved 6-helix bundle thought to harbor the ion translocation site.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: In EcNhaA and other CPA2 antiporters, the ion-binding and transport site has been proposed to include two conserved aspartates.
source: In EcNhaA and other CPA2 antiporters, the ion-binding and transport site has been proposed to include two conserved aspartates (Inoue et al., 1995; Hunte et al., 2005; Maes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: In the CPA1 antiporters, one of the aspartates is replaced by an asparagine, which likewise is thought to participate in ion-binding and translocation.
source: In the CPA1 antiporters, one of the aspartates is replaced by an asparagine, which likewise is thought to participate in ion-binding and translocation (Hellmer et al., 2003; Goswami et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: In the EcNhaA X-ray structure the two conserved aspartates are located at the center of TMH V.
source: In the EcNhaA X-ray structure (Hunte et al., 2005) the two conserved aspartates are located at the center of TMH V, which means that the corresponding residues in MjNhaP1 are in TMH 6.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: The corresponding residues to the conserved aspartates in EcNhaA are in TMH 6 of MjNhaP1.
source: In the EcNhaA X-ray structure (Hunte et al., 2005) the two conserved aspartates are located at the center of TMH V, which means that the corresponding residues in MjNhaP1 are in TMH 6.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural comparison.

claim: TMH 6 of MjNhaP1 participates prominently in Na+-induced changes.
source: Our difference maps show that this helix participates prominently in Na+-induced changes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data.

claim: Changes were found in helix 5e of MjNhaP1, which corresponds to the periplasmic half of TMH IV of EcNhaA.
source: We also found changes in helix 5e of MjNhaP1, which corresponds to the periplasmic half of TMH IV of EcNhaA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data and structural comparison.

claim: Electron crystallography of 2D crystals, side-directed tryptophan fluorescence, ion accessibility studies and MD simulations have all found conformational changes or an intrinsically high degree of flexibility in the periplasmic half of TMH IV of EcNhaA.
source: Electron crystallography of 2D crystals, side-directed tryptophan fluorescence, ion accessibility studies and MD simulations have all found conformational changes or an intrinsically high degree of flexibility in this half helix (Appel et al., 2009; Kozachkov and Padan, 2011; Rimon et al., 2012), and we find that the corresponding region in MjNhaP1 also moves or rearranges upon Na+ binding.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: The corresponding region in MjNhaP1 also moves or rearranges upon Na+ binding.
source: Electron crystallography of 2D crystals, side-directed tryptophan fluorescence, ion accessibility studies and MD simulations have all found conformational changes or an intrinsically high degree of flexibility in this half helix (Appel et al., 2009; Kozachkov and Padan, 2011; Rimon et al., 2012), and we find that the corresponding region in MjNhaP1 also moves or rearranges upon Na+ binding.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data.

claim: The events known to occur upon ion-binding and translocation in EcNhaA are consistent with the conformational changes observed in MjNhaP1.
source: The events known to occur upon ion-binding and translocation in EcNhaA are thus consistent with the conformational changes we observe in MjNhaP1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the comparison.

claim: The 3 Å X-ray structure of the Na+/H+ antiporter NapA from T. thermophilus has been reported.
source: Recently, the 3 Å X-ray structure of the Na+/H+ antiporter NapA from T. thermophilus has been reported (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: TtNapA is electrogenic, and thus functionally similar to EcNhaA.
source: TtNapA is electrogenic, and thus functionally similar to EcNhaA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: In terms of protein structure, TtNapA resembles MjNhaP1 much more closely than EcNhaA.
source: However, in terms of protein structure, it resembles MjNhaP1 much more closely, as judged from a 6 Å projection map we calculated from the TtNapA coordinates (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: TtNapA has 13 TMHs, similar to MjNhaP1, while EcNhaA has only 12.
source: This refers in particular to the position of the 6-helix bundle relative to the dimer interface and the number of TMHs (13 in TtNapA and MjNhaP1, only 12 in EcNhaA).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural comparison.

claim: Lee et al. assume that the structures of TtNapA and EcNhaA show the outward-open and inward-open conformation of essentially the same antiporter.
source: Nevertheless, Lee et al. assume that the structures of TtNapA and EcNhaA show the outward-open and inward-open conformation of essentially the same antiporter.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of Lee et al.'s interpretation.

claim: Lee et al. generated a model of TtNapA in the inward-open conformation based on the EcNhaA structure.
source: A model of TtNapA in the inward-open conformation based on the EcNhaA structure was generated, and compared it to the outward-open TtNapA structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of Lee et al.'s work.

claim: There were major differences between the inward-open model and the outward-open structure of TtNapA, in particular with respect to the position and orientation of the 6-helix bundle.
source: Not surprisingly, there were major differences between the inward-open model and the outward-open structure, in particular with respect to the position and orientation of the 6-helix bundle, which appeared to rotate by 20° within the membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of Lee et al.'s findings.

claim: The 6-helix bundle appeared to rotate by 20° within the membrane in the comparison between inward-open and outward-open TtNapA.
source: Not surprisingly, there were major differences between the inward-open model and the outward-open structure, in particular with respect to the position and orientation of the 6-helix bundle, which appeared to rotate by 20° within the membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of Lee et al.'s findings.

claim: Lee et al. proposed a transport mechanism based on the TtNapA comparison, which was claimed to apply to all Na+/H+ antiporters.
source: On the basis of this comparison, they proposed a transport mechanism, which was claimed to apply to all Na+/H+ antiporters.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of Lee et al.'s claims.

claim: A massive domain movement is difficult to reconcile with the high turnover rates of EcNhaA and the comparatively subtle substrate-induced changes in and around the 6-helix bundle observed experimentally in MjNhaP1.
source: However, such a massive domain movement is difficult to reconcile with the high turnover rates of EcNhaA and the comparatively subtle substrate-induced changes in and around the 6-helix bundle we observe experimentally in MjNhaP1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a critique of Lee et al.'s model.

claim: The very large and strong difference peaks in the region of the 6-helix bundle in the TtNapA comparison bear no resemblance to the experimental difference maps of MjNhaP1.
source: The very large and strong difference peaks in the region of the 6-helix bundle bear no resemblance to Figures 4 and 5.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: A 20º in-plane rotation of the 6-helix bundle does not occur in MjNhaP1.
source: We conclude that a 20º in-plane rotation of the 6-helix bundle does not occur in MjNhaP1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the data comparison.

claim: A 20º in-plane rotation of the 6-helix bundle most likely also does not occur in EcNhaA.
source: It most likely also does not occur in EcNhaA, since Figure 5—figure supplement 2 also bears no resemblance to projection difference maps obtained under a range of physiological ion and pH conditions with this antiporter (Appel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: The projection and difference maps indicate two different conformations of MjNhaP1: one in the absence of Na+, and one in the presence of Na+ above 20 mM at pH 8 or 200 mM at pH 4.
source: The projection and difference maps in Figures 3–5 indicate two different conformations of MjNhaP1: one in the absence of Na+, which looks similar at any pH between 4 and 8, and one in the presence of Na+ above 20 mM at pH 8 or 200 mM at pH 4.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data.

claim: The conformation in the absence of Na+ looks similar at any pH between 4 and 8.
source: The projection and difference maps in Figures 3–5 indicate two different conformations of MjNhaP1: one in the absence of Na+, which looks similar at any pH between 4 and 8, and one in the presence of Na+ above 20 mM at pH 8 or 200 mM at pH 4.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data.

claim: The conformation in the presence of Na+ shows the Na+-bound state.
source: The latter shows the Na+-bound state, whereas the former shows the apo or proton-bound state of the antiporter.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The conformation in the absence of Na+ shows the apo or proton-bound state of the antiporter.
source: The latter shows the Na+-bound state, whereas the former shows the apo or proton-bound state of the antiporter.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: At elevated Na+ concentrations, the pH 6 maps resemble those at pH 4 or 8, but the difference peaks are less distinct and only roughly half as strong.
source: At elevated Na+ concentrations, the pH 6 maps resemble those at pH 4 or 8, but the difference peaks are less distinct and only roughly half as strong, as would be expected if the corresponding helices were disordered.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data.

claim: The apparent disorder at pH 6 is ascribed to the fact that the antiporter is fully active at pH 6, and the helices involved in ion translocation would oscillate between the sodium-free and sodium-bound state.
source: We ascribe this apparent disorder to the fact that the antiporter is fully active at pH 6, and the helices involved in ion translocation would oscillate between the sodium-free and sodium-bound state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: When the 2D crystals are frozen in liquid nitrogen, the helices are trapped in a continuum of slightly different orientations.
source: Hence, when the 2D crystals are frozen in liquid nitrogen, the helices are trapped in a continuum of slightly different orientations.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for the observed disorder.

claim: In a projection map, which takes the average of all molecules on the 2D crystal lattice, the helices would appear disordered.
source: In a projection map, which takes the average of all molecules on the 2D crystal lattice, the helices would thus appear disordered, as observed.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for the observed disorder.

claim: At pH 4 and 8 MjNhaP1 is down-regulated and presumably more or less rigid.
source: At pH 4 and 8 MjNhaP1 is down-regulated (Vinothkumar et al., 2005) and presumably more or less rigid.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: Under pH 4 and 8 conditions, the effect of Na+ on the structure is progressive, indicating that the maps are averages of an increasing number of molecules in the Na+-bound state and a decreasing number in the apo state, as the Na+ concentration increases.
source: Under these conditions, the effect of Na+ on the structure is progressive, indicating that the maps are averages of an increasing number of molecules on the 2D crystal lattice in the Na+-bound state and a decreasing number in the apo state, as the Na+ concentration increases.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The height of the difference peaks is a direct measure of Na+ affinity.
source: The height of the difference peaks is then a direct measure of Na+ affinity, and enables us to determine apparent binding constants for Na+ in different pH regimes (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: MjNhaP1 is down-regulated at pH 8.
source: We (Goswami et al., 2011) and others (Hellmer et al., 2002) have shown that MjNhaP1 is down-regulated at pH 8.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: Down-regulation of MjNhaP1 at acidic pH has not yet been shown experimentally.
source: Down-regulation at acidic pH has not yet been shown experimentally (largely because there is no suitable pH-sensitive fluorescent dye), but follows from physiological considerations, which indicate that the antiporter must be inactive at pH 4 to prevent uncontrolled influx of Na+ ions that would otherwise result from a large outward pH gradient (Vinothkumar et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The antiporter must be inactive at pH 4 to prevent uncontrolled influx of Na+ ions that would otherwise result from a large outward pH gradient.
source: Down-regulation at acidic pH has not yet been shown experimentally (largely because there is no suitable pH-sensitive fluorescent dye), but follows from physiological considerations, which indicate that the antiporter must be inactive at pH 4 to prevent uncontrolled influx of Na+ ions that would otherwise result from a large outward pH gradient (Vinothkumar et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: A shutdown at acidic and basic conditions is a key feature of the simple kinetic model proposed by Mager et al. for EcNhaA.
source: A shutdown at acidic and basic conditions is a key feature of the simple kinetic model proposed by Mager et al. for EcNhaA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The simple kinetic model proposed by Mager et al. for EcNhaA also appears to hold for MjNhaP1.
source: This model thus also appears to hold for MjNhaP1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data.

claim: At pH 4, MjNhaP1 may be down-regulated due to competition of H+ and Na+ for a common binding site.
source: At pH 4, this antiporter may be down-regulated due to competition of H+ and Na+ for a common binding site, and at pH 8 due to proton depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: At pH 8, MjNhaP1 may be down-regulated due to proton depletion.
source: At pH 4, this antiporter may be down-regulated due to competition of H+ and Na+ for a common binding site, and at pH 8 due to proton depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: Together with the activity peak around pH 6, these two effects would result in a bell-shaped pH dependence of transport activity.
source: Together with the activity peak around pH 6, these two effects would result in a bell-shaped pH dependence of transport activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: The observed 10-fold increase in apparent KD for Na+ from pH 8 to pH 4 is consistent with a competition of Na+ and H+ for a common binding site.
source: The observed 10-fold increase in apparent KDNa+ from pH 8 to pH 4 is consistent with a competition of Na+ and H+ for a common binding site, because more Na+ ions are needed to displace the protons as the H+ concentration rises.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: More Na+ ions are needed to displace the protons as the H+ concentration rises.
source: The observed 10-fold increase in apparent KDNa+ from pH 8 to pH 4 is consistent with a competition of Na+ and H+ for a common binding site, because more Na+ ions are needed to displace the protons as the H+ concentration rises.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for the observed pH dependence.

claim: In addition to substrate competition, the transport rate of MjNhaP1 is also modulated in some other way, for example by the protonation states of amino acid sidechains involved in ion-binding and translocation.
source: Apparently, in addition to substrate competition, the transport rate of MjNhaP1 is also modulated in some other way, for example by the protonation states of amino acid sidechains involved in ion-binding and translocation that render the antiporter more flexible at pH 6 than at pH 4 or pH 8.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: The protonation states of amino acid sidechains may render the antiporter more flexible at pH 6 than at pH 4 or pH 8.
source: Apparently, in addition to substrate competition, the transport rate of MjNhaP1 is also modulated in some other way, for example by the protonation states of amino acid sidechains involved in ion-binding and translocation that render the antiporter more flexible at pH 6 than at pH 4 or pH 8.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: In EcNhaA and NHE1, a pH sensor is thought to transform the antiporters from an active into an acid-locked state at low pH.
source: In EcNhaA and NHE1, a pH sensor is thought to transform the antiporters from an active into an acid-locked state at low pH (Aronson et al., 1982; Aronson, 1985; Taglicht et al., 1991; Wakabayashi et al., 2003; Padan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: In the case of EcNhaA, the pH sensor has been reported to involve a conformational switch at the level of secondary structure.
source: In the case of EcNhaA, this has been reported to involve a conformational switch at the level of secondary structure (Herz et al., 2010; Diab et al., 2011; Schushan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: In MjNhaP1, there is no evidence of a pH-triggered conformational switch.
source: In MjNhaP1, we see no evidence of a pH-triggered conformational switch (Figure 3), so that down-regulation at low pH is not associated with a significant change in secondary structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data.

claim: Down-regulation at low pH in MjNhaP1 is not associated with a significant change in secondary structure.
source: In MjNhaP1, we see no evidence of a pH-triggered conformational switch (Figure 3), so that down-regulation at low pH is not associated with a significant change in secondary structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental data.

claim: Down-regulation at low pH in MjNhaP1 may involve the re-orientation of amino acid sidechains, which would not be visible at 6 Å resolution.
source: However, it may involve the re-orientation of amino acid sidechains, which would not be visible at 6 Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation.

claim: Vinothkumar et al. investigated pH-induced changes in 2D crystals of MjNhaP1 in an earlier study.
source: In an earlier study, Vinothkumar et al. investigated pH-induced changes in 2D crystals of MjNhaP1 (Vinothkumar et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation.

claim: The crystals in the Vinothkumar et al. study had been grown in the presence of NaCl, and incubating them in salt-free buffers changed both the pH and the Na+ concentration simultaneously.
source: The crystals had been grown in the presence of NaCl, and therefore incubating them in salt-free buffers changed both the pH and the Na+ concentration simultaneously.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of the earlier study.

claim: The effect observed by Vinothkumar et al. was due to both Na+ and pH, rather than to pH only.
source: The effect observed by Vinothkumar et al. was thus due to both Na+ and pH, rather than to pH only.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the earlier study.

claim: The differences observed by Vinothkumar et al. were reproduced with 2D crystals grown with or without NaCl.
source: We were able to reproduce these differences with 2D crystals grown with or without NaCl, as indicated in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: By growing 2D crystals of MjNhaP1 in absence of sodium, it was possible to separate effects of the two substrate ions, Na+ and H+, on its conformation.
source: By growing 2D crystals of the archaeal Na+/H+ antiporter MjNhaP1 in absence of sodium, we were able to separate effects of the two substrate ions, Na+ and H+, on its conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a summary of the approach.

claim: This contrasts with current models of Na+/H+ antiporter regulation, which postulate a significant pH-triggered conformational switch.
source: This contrasts with current models of Na+/H+ antiporter regulation, which postulate a significant pH-triggered conformational switch.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a comparison with existing models.

claim: If a pH switch occurs in MjNhaP1, it does not affect the secondary structure but may involve sidechain movements, which are not resolved by the method used.
source: If such a pH switch occurs in MjNhaP1, it does not affect the secondary structure but may involve sidechain movements, which are not resolved by our method.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a qualification of the findings.

claim: At pH 8 and 4, where MjNhaP1 is down-regulated, the Na+-induced differences reflect a progressive change in the relative population of the two distinct conformational sodium-free and sodium-bound states.
source: At pH 8 and 4, where MjNhaP1 is down-regulated, the Na+-induced differences reflect a progressive change in the relative population of the two distinct conformational sodium-free and sodium-bound states.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: This enabled deduction of apparent binding constants of MjNhaP1 for Na+ under acidic and basic conditions.
source: This enabled us to deduce apparent binding constants of MjNhaP1 for Na+ under acidic and basic conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a summary of the findings.

claim: At pH 6, where MjNhaP1 is fully active, the helices involved in ion translocation appear disordered, due to averaging over many slightly different conformations on the crystal lattice.
source: At pH 6, where this antiporter is fully active, the helices involved in ion translocation appear disordered, due to averaging over many slightly different conformations on the crystal lattice.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The MjNhaP1 model allows the conclusion that the helix movements change the access to the proposed substrate binding site.
source: The MjNhaP1 model (Goswami et al., 2011) allows us to conclude that the helix movements deduced from the projection difference maps in Figures 4 and 5 change the access to the proposed substrate binding site, as shown schematically in Figure 7.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section and illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: In the apo or proton-bound state, the ion-binding site near the center of TMH 6 would be accessible from the extracellular side, making this the outward-open state.
source: In the apo or proton-bound state, the ion-binding site near the center of TMH 6 would be accessible from the extracellular side, making this the outward-open state.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: The helix movements brought about by Na+ ions convert the antiporter into the Na+-bound, inward-open state.
source: The helix movements brought about by Na+ ions then convert the antiporter into the Na+-bound, inward-open state.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: Oscillation between the two states would result in Na+/H+ antiport, as specified by the alternating access mechanism.
source: Oscillation between the two states would result in Na+/H+ antiport, as specified by the alternating access mechanism (Jardetzky, 1966).
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section and supported by a citation.

claim: It is likely that the mammalian NHE antiporters, which share many similarities with the archaeal Na+/H+ exchangers, work in the same way.
source: It is likely that the mammalian NHE antiporters, which share many similarities with the archaeal Na+/H+ exchangers, work in the same way.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusions section as a speculation based on the similarities.
